svg.title: Treaty of Versailles Territorial Losses (June 1919) & Occupation of the Ruhr (January 1923)
svg.desc: Historical GIS atlas map comparing 1914 Imperial Germany with the post-Versailles Weimar Republic, highlighting Germany’s 13% European territorial losses (Alsace-Lorraine, Eupen-Malmedy, North Schleswig, Posen and the Polish Corridor splitting East Prussia from mainland Germany, Free City of Danzig, Memel, and Eastern Upper Silesia), the 15-year League-administered Saar Coalfield, the 50 km Demilitarised Rhineland, and the January 1923 Franco-Belgian Occupation of the Ruhr.

text.tspan: Returned June 1919 • 75% of iron ore lost
Plebiscite cedes northern zone to Denmark
To Poland • Splits East Prussia from Reich
Vital coal & steel basin partitioned to Poland

svg.text: EDEXCEL GCSE HISTORY • PAPER 3 (OPTION 31): WEIMAR & NAZI GERMANY, 1918–39
Treaty of Versailles Territorial Losses (1919) & Occupation of the Ruhr (1923)
Versailles (28 Jun 1919) imposed Article 231 War Guilt, £6.6bn reparations, a 100,000-man army cap, and stripped 13% of European territory.
Defaulting on coal reparations triggered the Jan 1923 Franco-Belgian Ruhr invasion; passive resistance & money-printing sparked hyperinflation.
